..
A nearly-stationary col as well as upper-level divergence has
maintained the convectively active, wet pattern today. After 
midnight, a lull in showers and light northerlies may allow for 
enough clearing for scattered, island-effect rainfall Monday 
afternoon. Due to the slow-moving nature of the convergence zone, 
isolated thunderstorms are possible through Monday. Then, drier 
conditions are possible for a few subsequent forecast periods as the
active weather pattern exits the region to the northwest. As for the
latter half of the week, northerlies may increase in speed to light 
to gentle. Shower coverage may differ as model guidance hints at a 
potential circulation developing to the east of the islands. Due to 
the high uncertainty regarding this pattern, showers top out at 30 
percent through Saturday with a slight chance of thunderstorms 
returning. This will continue to be refined as confidence naturally 
increases with time. Shortly thereafter, a dry spell is possible 
entering early next week.

Marine...
The westerly swell continues to subside, allowing for combined seas
to drop to 3 to 5 ft tonight, followed by another decrease to 3 to 4
ft Monday. Light to gentle northwesterlies will shift to the north
Monday and eventually to the northeast later in the week. There is a
moderate risk of rip currents along north, south, and west facing
reefs, with the former two dropping to a low risk beginning Monday. 
Island-effect showers may be a concern Monday afternoon for southern
coastal waters.

Eastern Micronesia...
Very little change to the previous forecast. Maintained isolated
showers at Pohnpei and Kosrae through Monday night. A re-invigorated
monsoon trough is expected to bring increased showers to Majuro 
later this evening, ending the dry pattern there. This will initiate
an overall unsettled pattern spreading across eastern Micronesia 
that will continue across the Marshalls through the end of the week.
The convection will spread west over the next day, bringing this 
pattern to Kosrae and Pohnpei Tuesday. This pattern will then
continue through the end of the week.

No major changes were made to the marine forecast. Seas could climb
to as high as 7 feet after midweek. Light to gentle winds will become
gentle to moderate at Kosrae Monday, then become moderate to fresh
around midweek and remain there through at least Friday. Pohnpei will
see gentle to moderate winds Tuesday that will continue through the
end of the week. For Majuro, winds will become light to moderate 
Monday, returning to light to gentle by midweek.

Western Micronesia...
A ridge extending from a buffer circulation near West Papua is still
inducing some diffluent flow over Yap and Palau, leading to quiet
conditions over the next few days. During this period of drier 
weather, haze sourced from distant wildfires in Indonesia are 
expected to continue across Palau and Yap. Scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms are found across the far southern islands of
Palau, closer to the buffer circulation, however this area of showers
is not expected to build farther north. A broader area of showers 
and a few thunderstorms are spread out across across Chuuk State and 
eastern Yap State due to moderate northwesterly convergence alongside
the monsoon trough and a monsoon disturbance between Chuuk and 
Pohnpei. The monsoon disturbance is expected to move in a general 
west-northwest direction in the coming days and remain fairly 
disorganized, however, the strengthening convergence along the 
western and southern peripheries will be the focus of unsettled 
weather for the region this week. As the disturbance shifts west-
northwestward, scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are 
expected to continue through Monday at Chuuk. Showers then taper down
to isolated to scattered Monday night and Tuesday. As the monsoon 
trough reorients itself this week, southwesterly convergence begins 
to set up across Chuuk around Wednesday, bringing another increase in
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms towards the latter half
of week. Overall, Yap and Palau remain on the outskirts of this 
developing pattern, but depending on the proximity of the monsoon 
trough, low-end scattered showers may return to Yap Wednesday and 
Thursday, and to Palau sometime late week. 

Latest altimetry data shows combined seas have remain steady at 2 to
4 feet near Palau and Yap, and 3 to 5 feet at Chuuk. Benign marine 
conditions are expected to continue over the next several days, with 
seas increasing to 4 to 6 feet around Thursday for Chuuk coastal 
waters due to an increase in south to southeast swell. Light to 
gentle winds persist over the next several days with an increase in 
gentle to moderate southwesterly winds at Chuuk starting Wednesday.
